title: The rule-complexity threshold for complex behavior is very low

fields.label: Label
fields.value: The rule-complexity threshold for complex behavior is very low

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Systems with sufficiently simple rules show only repetition, slightly more complicated rules often add nesting, and complex behavior requires crossing a threshold in rule complexity, but in every kind of system studied this threshold is extremely low.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 3: The World of Simple Programs

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The remarkable discovery that we have made, however, is that this threshold is typically extremely low.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 3, “The World of Simple Programs”; section “Some Conclusions” (from p. 105), p. 106. Scope: all kinds of simple programs

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch03-19: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.47

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Bounded rule spaces can be enumerated and thresholds estimated for selected formalisms. The as-stated claim ranges over every system kind and uses encoding-dependent notions, so current computation can resolve only restricted cases.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For several formally specified system families, order rules by a declared description-length measure and classify long-run behavior using fixed complexity criteria. Estimate the first complexity-producing rule and its percentile within each family.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Long transients and undecidability obstruct behavioral classification.

Rule complexity depends on encoding.

Every kind of system is not finitely surveyable.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.25
operationalizability: 0.38
analysis feasibility: 0.5
data existence: 0.68
discriminating power: 0.48

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: For the concrete classes in the chapter, the smallest rule that leaves repetition and nesting is a computable statistic, and several of those spaces are fully enumerable with public software. The claim that the threshold is extremely low in every kind of system still needs a shared scale of rule complexity, and different scales move the threshold. Existing enumerations can test the chapter's classes under an explicit scale, not the unqualified general principle.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Order rules in each studied class by description length and record the shortest rule whose evolution is neither periodic nor nested under a fixed classifier. A first complex rule at very small size in every class supports an extremely low threshold; complexity appearing only at large description length in some class would refute that class.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Some rule spaces are small enough to exhaust, but others can only be sampled.

'Extremely low' and 'complex' depend on the complexity measure and the behavior classifier.

analysis feasibility: 0.7
data existence: 0.75
operationalizability: 0.55
